explanation: Potsdam left Germany divided into zones under four administrations with no agreed future, and the four years that followed — the failure of the councils of foreign ministers, the currency reform, the Berlin blockade — turned the provisional line into a frontier. The Atlantic treaty of April 1949 is the western answer to that, and it is the door through which Portugal, a dictatorship that had spent the war neutral and had been kept out of the United Nations, entered the western system as a founder member. The claim is about the sequence from a deferred German question to a standing alliance, not that Potsdam was intended to produce one.
